question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Rock the boat
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"rock the boat"** means to disturb a stable situation or to cause trouble where none is wanted. (स्थिर स्थिति को बाधित करना)

 
 
• **Example:** He didn't want to ***rock the boat*** by voicing his opinion during the meeting.
 
 
 
• **"Disturb a stable situation"** refers to causing trouble or changes in a situation that is currently peaceful or functioning well. (स्थिर स्थिति को बाधित करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The new policy might** *disturb a stable situation*** in the company, leading to employee dissatisfaction.
 
 

Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is ' ***To* disturb a stable situation**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Pester and irritate someone **(किसी को परेशान और चिढ़ाना): To annoy someone repeatedly.

 
 
• **Example:** The little boy would often ***pester and irritate*** his sister by asking too many questions.
 
 
 
• **Overcome a difficult situation **(कठिन स्थिति पर काबू पाना): To successfully deal with a challenging scenario.
 
 
• **Example:** She managed to ***overcome a difficult situatio***n by staying calm and focused.
 
 
 
• **Divert someone’s attention **(किसी का ध्यान भटकाना): To cause someone to stop paying attention to something and focus on something else.
 
 
• **Example:** He tried to ***divert her attention*** by asking an unrelated question.
